title: Check: your practice cluster
description: Five questions on kind, minikube and the habits the exam rewards.

questions.prompt: What does kind use to run cluster nodes?
questions.explanation: kind is 'Kubernetes IN Docker': each node is a container, which makes multi-node clusters cheap to create and throw away.

questions.prompt: On a local cluster a `type: LoadBalancer` Service keeps `<pending>` as its external IP. Why?

options.text: There is no cloud controller to provision a load balancer
The cluster has run out of node ports

questions.explanation: That is correct behaviour, not a bug. Locally you reach the Service with NodePort, `kubectl port-forward` or `minikube tunnel`.

questions.prompt: Write the command that shows which cluster your kubectl is pointing at right now.
questions.explanation: Getting this wrong on the exam means doing correct work in the wrong cluster. Check it before you start.

questions.prompt: The lesson stresses one habit because the exam is only two hours long. Which?

options.text: Setting up aliases and autocompletion in the first minute

questions.explanation: Two hours is not much. The setup that saves keystrokes pays for itself many times over, and the same habits belong in your practice cluster.

questions.prompt: Which are good reasons to run a local cluster while studying? Choose all that apply.

options.text: You can break things on purpose and diagnose them
It is the only way to read the documentation
You can practise the commands until they are muscle memory
You can throw the cluster away and start clean

questions.explanation: The exam is a terminal. Reading about a command is not the same as having typed it a hundred times.
